cards.title: Be worth + -ing
cards.summary: Significa que algo «vale la pena». Después de worth va un sustantivo o un verbo con -ing.
cards.form: be worth + sustantivo / verbo-ing · it's worth + verbo-ing
uses: Recomendar: The museum is worth visiting.
Valorar un esfuerzo: It's worth the effort.
Valor en dinero: This painting is worth a lot of money.
En negativo: It isn't worth it.

pitfalls.wrong: This book is worth to read.
pitfalls.why: Después de worth va -ing, no to + verbo.
Worth no es un verbo: se usa con be (it's worth, it isn't worth).

pitfalls.wrong: This book is worth reading it.
pitfalls.why: El objeto ya es el sujeto (this book): no se repite con it después del verbo en -ing.

examples.es: Vale la pena visitar el museo.
Vale la pena leer este libro.

examples.en: It isn't worth waiting for the bus.
examples.es: No vale la pena esperar el autobús.

examples.en: Their old house is worth a lot of money now.
examples.es: Su casa vieja vale mucho dinero ahora.

cards.title: Used to, be used to y get used to
cards.summary: Used to + verbo habla de hábitos del pasado. Be used to + -ing significa «estar acostumbrado a» y get used to + -ing, «acostumbrarse a».
cards.form: used to + verbo base · be used to + sustantivo / -ing · get used to + sustantivo / -ing
uses: Used to: algo que hacías antes y ya no (I used to live in Lima).
Be used to: algo que ya es normal para ti (I'm used to working at night).
Get used to: el proceso de acostumbrarse (You'll get used to the cold).
En be used to y get used to, to es preposición: después va -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I am used to work at night.
pitfalls.right: I am used to working at night.
pitfalls.why: En be used to, to es preposición: va seguido de -ing.

pitfalls.wrong: I use to play soccer when I was a kid.
pitfalls.right: I used to play soccer when I was a kid.
pitfalls.why: En oraciones afirmativas, el hábito pasado es used to (con -d).

pitfalls.wrong: Did you used to live here?
pitfalls.right: Did you use to live here?
pitfalls.why: Con did se usa use to (sin -d).

pitfalls.wrong: I can't accustom to the weather.
pitfalls.right: I can't get used to the weather.
pitfalls.why: «Acostumbrarse a» algo se dice get used to.
